line:
"Brann, keep working that brass ring with whatever oil you have, I'll come back for it." I leave the reliquary seated in the socket, drop down the trapdoor, and take the third step above the doorway just as the crate gives.

As the first pikemen crowd Kit's shield, I cast Faerie Fire at the doorway and the shingle beyond, outlining all of them in light so Kit's attacks have advantage, and call, "Hit the lit ones, Kit, and tell me when you need Healing Word."

The crate gives with a crack and the door bursts inward. Three pikemen crowd the doorway in the grey light, and the order of turns puts them ahead of you.

Two long pike-points stab at Kit. Both hit, 2 and 7, and the blood shows dark on her tabard. She grunts, drops her shoulder behind the shield, and answers with her longsword. Her blow opens the first pikeman's arm to the bone, and he reels back, barely on his feet. The third pikeman is hemmed in behind his fellows, looking for a way past.

Then it's your turn, on the third step. You throw out your hand and cast Faerie Fire, one slot, and a shimmer of blue light bursts over the doorway and the shingle beyond. It doesn't catch everyone. The two men at the door twist aside in time. Only the third, jostling behind them, is caught, and he's now outlined in blue fire, dim light spilling off him. Attacks against him have advantage as long as you hold your concentration. You have one 1st-level slot left. Kit is hurt but upright, with your Inspiration die still on her. Sparrow and the grey-cloaked man are staying back on the shingle, out of the light.

You have used your action. Your bonus action and your movement are still yours this turn. What does Wren do?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

features: Darkvision: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Fey Ancestry: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.
Skill Versatility: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

Bardic Inspiration (d6): You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.  Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. At level 2: Bardic Inspiration die d6.
Jack of All Trades: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 10 ~7:30 AM: fight at the north door of the Gullspit light. Sparrow (hand crossbow) and three Vantry-grey-less pikemen (Guards 1-3) attack; Kit holds the doorway; Wren's Faerie Fire failed (all saved) and she was shot to 9 HP. The Grey Cloak himself stays outside and has not yet acted.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Grey Cloak

The crate gives with a crack, and the door bursts inward. Kit takes the doorway with her shield up and Guard 1 and Guard 2 jabbing at her from the shingle. You drop down to the third step above the doorway.

Round 1. Sparrow hangs back behind his pikemen and fires a hand-crossbow past them, and the bolt skips off Kit's shield. You cast Faerie Fire over the doorway and the shingle. The light pours out in blue, but every one of them throws himself clear: the three guards and Sparrow all made their saves, so only the splintered door-frame and the crate glow. Guard 1's pike finds a gap and bites Kit for 6. Guard 2's goes wide. Kit's longsword misses, so she hums your bar of the road song, and the Inspiration die you gave her adds a 4 that turns the miss into a hit. She opens Guard 1's arm for 6, and he is hurt but standing.

Round 2. Sparrow's second bolt comes up the stair, and this one finds you: 8 points. You drop to 9 hit points, and the pain breaks your concentration (a 9 against DC 10). Faerie Fire gutters out. You've one 1st-level slot left and two uses of Inspiration.

Kit is down to 12 hit points, still in the doorway. Guard 1 is bloodied. Guard 2 and Guard 3 are unhurt. Sparrow stands ten feet behind them, smiling, with the Grey Cloak still unseen beyond. It is your turn on the third step.

What does Wren do?

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

You call out your challenge, clear and carrying, and the road goes very still. Then Sparrow's smile slides, and the fight starts before your staff is even up.

Sparrow wins the first move and fires his hand crossbow at you. He rolls a 1 on the die, and the bolt skitters off the wagon-bed. Kit answers with her crossbow and hits him for 4, so he's hurt but nowhere near done. The five pikemen come in a rush down the narrow road. One of them rolls a natural 20 on Kit and the critical hit takes 10 from her, so she's at 10 of 20. Another misses her. A third lunges at you on Ember and rolls a 1 of his own. The last two are jammed behind their friends on the narrow road and can't get past. The Grey Cloak hasn't moved. He stands back in the sun with his hood up, watching you, one hand turning that green ring.

Now it's your turn. The lamp-staff is still upright in your hand, Pell's guards are waiting in the reeds for it to go up, and Faerie Fire is ready on your tongue. Three pikemen are on you and Kit, Sparrow and two more are behind them in a bunch within a single 20-foot cube, and the Grey Cloak is a little farther back. You've three slots and three Bardic Inspirations, and your bonus action is free.

Do you raise the staff and cast as you said, and is there anything you want to add with your bonus action?
